title: Using Curiosity Gaps to Drive Views and Followers
summary: This post explains how using curiosity gaps can turn ordinary social media videos into viral content that gains both views and long-term followers. By introducing an unanswered rating suspense in a single video and an ongoing challenge word like 'until', creators compel viewers to watch to the end and subscribe for future updates.
key_points: Curiosity gaps sell: Framing simple actions (e.g., 'packing my dad's lunch until he rates one a 10/10') creates psychological suspense that outperforms basic descriptions.
First gap (Watch time): Setting up an expected score or verdict creates an immediate curiosity gap that keeps viewers watching until the very end.
Second gap (Follows): Words like 'until' turn an isolated video into an ongoing quest or series, motivating viewers to follow to see the eventual outcome.
Step 1: Open a question your audience needs answered (e.g., 'what's the end score', 'who's the winner', 'can I actually do this?').
Step 2: Save the answer for the end of the video, ideally hinging on your expert abilities.
Step 3: To gain followers, extend the question across multiple videos via a long-term goal, competition, or repeatable series.
Example for Contractors: '3 contractors quoted the same kitchen. One of them was $40K off – can you guess which?' (reveal teaches how to compare quotes).
Example for Skincare: 'I tested the 3 most viral acne hacks on one side of my face. One of them made it worse' (reveal positions your product).
Example for Trainers: 'Can a 68-year-old do 10 real pushups in 8 weeks? Week 1' (viewer follows to track progress).
Fulfill your promises in the content to maintain trust with your audience.
content:
Post Caption:
How did a meal prep video get nearly 15 million views and help the creator grow over 400k followers?

Good ole human psychology 🙂

Here’s how you can use these strategies to get the right views and followers for your business.

You just need to put people in enough suspense that they can’t scroll past without an answer, and they want to stick around for more.

Here’s how👇

Step 1: Open a question your audience NEEDS answered. It can be “what’s the end score,” “what’s the final verdict,” “who’s the winner,” “what’ll the end result look like,” or “can I actually do this?”

Step 2: Save the answer for the end, and bonus points if it hinges on your expert abilities.

Step 3: If you want it to bring you more followers, make the question take more than one video to answer. It can be a long-term goal, a competition, or just a repeatable series.

Here’s what that can look like:

General contractor: “3 contractors quoted the same kitchen. One of them was $40K off – can you guess which?” (the reveal teaches buyers how to compare quotes)

Skincare brand: “I tested the 3 most viral acne hacks on one side of my face. One of them made it worse” (the reveal sets up your product as the solution)

Personal trainer: “Can a 68-year-old do 10 real pushups in 8 weeks? Week 1” (viewers follow to see the result)

Couples therapist: “I asked 100 couples the one question that predicts if they’ll make it. Here’s what the happiest ones said” (the reveal shows your expertise)

Just make sure your video is centered around your products and services, and that you fulfill your promises to avoid losing trust with your audience :)

Happy creating!✨

Creator featured: @flowcookofficial

Transcript:
"This video proves that gaps sell. This creator could have said 'packing my dad's lunch' and gotten a couple thousand views, but instead they got nearly 15 million views by adding two elements of psychology. The first that gets us to watch, and the second one that gets us to follow. First, this rating sets up the expectation that their dad is going to give the meal a score. That opens up a curiosity gap in our brains where now we need to know what is he going to rate it, and we're going to watch to the end to find out. Second, one word gets us to want to follow. Most people would have focused on the suspense for that one meal, but this creator got us hooked and wanting to watch every single video moving forward by using this one word. Did you spot it yet? The word 'until' creates another curiosity gap where now we have to follow to figure out which meal is going to be rated a 10 out of 10. How can you use this for your business? See the c-"
